pages.title: Introduction
pages.content:
## Welcome to the Kitchen

Kitchen turns farming and food into a hobby of its own. Plant rice in a flooded field, harvest tea in a cherry grove, cut fish on a cutting board and cook a bowl of ramen over a fire. Then do what makes it special: put the dish on the table and let your friends eat from it, bite by bite. Everything works in the normal game, no mods needed.

### What you will do

* **Grow.** Ten new crops grow in the wild and on your farmland: rice, soybeans, napa cabbage, green onion, daikon, tea, corn, tomato, chili peppers and sesame. Picking a ripe crop with a right-click makes it grow back.
* **Prepare.** Use a knife on the Cutting Board, then cook in the Cooking Pot over a campfire or a Kamado Stove.
* **Share.** Sushi platters, ramen, bento boxes, dango and tea sets can be placed on a table. Every bite is its own little animation.
* **Decorate.** Tansu cabinets, baskets, crates, tatami mats and cushions make the kitchen yours.

### How the pages are organised

Start with **Crops** (where to find seeds), then **Stations** (how to cut and cook), then **Recipes** and **Shared Meals**. **Props** is the furniture page. Each crop, station, meal and prop has its own page.

### Good to know first

* Food is more than decoration: dishes give good effects, and a shared meal feeds a whole table.
* Kitchen works with Steamworks (flour, mochi, tofu in bulk), with Sakagura (drinks need Kitchen ingredients) and with Kura (store your crates in the network).
* The recipe book **/zukan** lists every cutting and cooking recipe.

### Start here

1. Read [Kitchen](/wiki?page=kitchen) for the one-minute explanation.
2. Find some wild seeds on the [Crops](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops) page.
3. Build a [Cutting Board and a Cooking Pot](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations) and cook your first meal.

pages.title: Kitchen
pages.content:
## Kitchen - Japanese farming and cooking

Kitchen adds new crops, cooking stations and Japanese dishes to Iekcorbar. Grow rice and soybeans, cut fish into sashimi, cook ramen in a clay pot over a fire, and put a sushi platter on the table for your friends to eat from piece by piece. You only need the normal game - no mods.

### How it works in one minute

1. **Find seeds.** Wild crops grow in the world (rice by swamps and rivers, tea in cherry groves and jungles, and so on). Break them for seeds.
2. **Plant them** on farmland like wheat. Rice needs wet farmland (water nearby).
3. **Cut** ingredients on a **Cutting Board** with a **knife**.
4. **Cook** meals in a **Cooking Pot** placed on a campfire, fire, lava, magma block or a lit **Kamado Stove**.
5. **Eat** dishes straight away, or **sneak + right-click** a block to put a meal down and share it.

### Pages

* [Crops](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops) - what grows where and how to harvest it
* [Stations](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations) - knives, Cutting Board, Cooking Pot, Kamado Stove
* [Recipes](/wiki?page=kitchen-recipes) - everything you can cut, cook and craft
* [Shared Meals](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals) - sushi platters, ramen, bento and tea sets
* [Props](/wiki?page=kitchen-props) - cabinet, basket, crates, rich soil, tatami and cushions

### Works with Steamworks

* Steamworks **flour** can replace wheat in noodles, soy sauce and tempura.
* A **millstone** grinds rice into flour, a **steam hammer** pounds steamed rice into mochi, and a heated **kettle + mixer** makes tofu and steamed rice in bulk.

Type **/kitchen** in game for a short help and a link back here.

pages.title: Kitchen Crops
pages.content:
## Crops

Kitchen crops grow on **farmland** (or [Rich Soil](/wiki?page=kitchen-props)) like wheat: they need light (level 9 or more) and only grow while the area is loaded. Bone meal speeds them up. A ripe crop can be **picked by right-clicking it** - it drops the harvest and starts growing again, so you don't have to replant.

* [Rice](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-rice)
* [Soybean](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-soybean)
* [Napa Cabbage](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-napa-cabbage)
* [Green Onion](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-green-onion)
* [Daikon](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-daikon)
* [Tea](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-tea)
* [Corn](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-corn)
* [Tomato](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-tomato)
* [Chili Pepper](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-chili-pepper)
* [Sesame](/wiki?page=kitchen-crops-sesame)

### Good to know

* **Rice** only grows on **wet** farmland (water within 4 blocks, like normal farmland hydration). On Rich Soil it needs water within 2 blocks.
* **Tea** is a bush: after picking it drops back to a young bush instead of starting from seed.
* **Corn** cuts on the Cutting Board into **Cornmeal** (for polenta and pickling).
* Breaking a young crop gives the seed back. Breaking a ripe one gives the harvest.
* Trampling the farmland pops the crop off, just like wheat.
* With a **knife**, breaking tall grass sometimes gives **Straw** (for bales, mats and compost).

pages.title: Kitchen Stations
pages.content:
## Stations

Stations are placed like blocks. Break them by hitting them a few times (one hit in creative); whatever is inside drops.


* [Knives](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations-knives)
* [Cutting Board](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations-cutting-board)
* [Cooking Pot](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations-cooking-pot)
* [Kamado Stove](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations-kamado-stove)

pages.title: Knives
pages.content:
| Knife | Recipe |
|---|---|
| Flint Knife | flint + stick (diagonal) |
| Iron Hocho | iron ingot + stick (diagonal) |
| Diamond Hocho | diamond + stick (diagonal) |
| Netherite Hocho | Diamond Hocho + netherite ingot in a smithing table |

Knives cut food on the Cutting Board and are light weapons.

Back to [Kitchen Stations](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations)

pages.title: Cutting Board
pages.content:
Recipe: **stick + 2 planks** in a row.

1. Right-click the board with an ingredient to put it on.
2. Right-click with a **knife** to cut it - the pieces pop out. Every cut uses a little knife durability.
3. Right-click with an empty hand to take it back.

Back to [Kitchen Stations](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations)

pages.title: Cooking Pot
pages.content:
Recipe: **iron ingot, stick, iron ingot** on top, **brick, empty, brick** in the middle, **3 bricks** at the bottom.

Put it **on a heat source**: campfire, fire, lava, magma block, a lit furnace or smoker, or a lit Kamado Stove. Right-click to open it:

* **6 ingredient slots** (left) - one item from each filled slot is used per dish.
* **Container slot** - bowls or glass bottles for soups and drinks.
* **Result slot** (right) - take the finished food out.

The clock in the middle tells you what is happening: cooking progress, "Needs heat", "Needs a bowl", or "No recipe with these ingredients". The pot keeps cooking while nobody looks inside, as long as the area is loaded.

Back to [Kitchen Stations](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations)

pages.title: Kamado Stove
pages.content:
Recipe: **3 bricks**, **brick, campfire, brick**, **3 cobblestone**.

* Light it with **flint and steel** (or a fire charge); put it out with a **water bucket** or a **shovel**.
* A lit stove **heats a Cooking Pot** placed on top of it.
* Without a pot on top it is a **grill**: right-click with raw food (anything a campfire can cook) to put up to 4 items on it. They cook twice as fast as on a campfire and pop off when done.

Back to [Kitchen Stations](/wiki?page=kitchen-stations)

pages.title: What the dishes do
pages.content:
* **Miso Soup, Oden, Nabe**: Regeneration for a few seconds.
* **Ramen, Gyudon, Oyakodon**: Regeneration plus Resistance for a minute.
* **Green Tea**: Speed for a minute and cures poison, hunger and nausea. You can always drink it.
* **Fugu Sashimi**: very filling and gives night vision... unless the cook got it wrong (15% poison).

Back to [Kitchen Recipes](/wiki?page=kitchen-recipes)

pages.title: Kitchen Shared Meals
pages.content:
## Shared Meals

Some dishes are meant to be put on the table. **Sneak + right-click the top of a block** to put one down. Anyone can then **right-click it to take a bite**: the chopsticks pick up one piece, you eat it, and the next person takes the next piece. Tea cups are lifted and drunk the same way.

* [Sushi Platter](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals-sushi-platter)
* [Ramen](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals-ramen)
* [Bento Box](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals-bento-box)
* [Dango Plate](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals-dango-plate)
* [Tea Set](/wiki?page=kitchen-shared-meals-tea-set)

### Good to know

* You can't take a bite when you're full - except tea: you can always drink tea (each cup gives Speed).
* The last bite of a ramen bowl also gives the ramen's Regeneration and Resistance.
* When the meal is finished the empty plate (or bowl) stays for a moment and then drops.
* **Hit** a meal to pick it up. An untouched meal comes back whole; a started one only gives the plate or bowl back.
* Meals can stand on any solid block, including Kitchen crates and cabinets.
